note: True for classic Kafka consumer groups: each partition is assigned to at most one consumer in a group, so consumer parallelism is capped by the partition count (KIP-932 calls this the 'coupling between the number of consumers in a consumer group and the number of partitions'). precise_version: In a classic Kafka consumer group, parallelism is capped by the number of partitions; Kafka 4.2+ share groups (queues) lift that cap.

note: Kafka itself is not slow (it is built for very high throughput). The bottleneck the teacher means is consumer parallelism: in a classic consumer group at most one consumer reads each partition, so per-recipient delivery work cannot be spread wider than the partition count, and very large partition counts carry their own costs. Kafka 4.2 share groups (production-ready Feb 2026) also relax this coupling.
precise_version: For massive fan-out, a Kafka consumer group alone limits delivery parallelism to the partition count, so per-user delivery work is usually handed to a queue that many workers can drain in parallel.

precise_version: On a successful response the browser looks at the first bytes of the body (the format signature, e.g. PNG's 89 50 4E 47...), picks the matching decoder and renders the pixels; SVG is identified by its Content-Type instead.

note: Not every browser decodes every format: MDN says 'Other than Safari, browsers do not natively support TIFF images in web content'. SVG is a vector XML format rendered by the browser's SVG engine rather than a raster decoder. PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and AVIF are broadly supported.
precise_version: Browsers ship decoders for the common web image formats (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, AVIF) and render SVG; TIFF works natively only in Safari.

PIL/Pillow does not use ImageMagick. Pillow ('the friendly PIL fork'; the original PIL is no longer maintained) is a C extension with its own imaging core that links codec libraries such as libjpeg, zlib, libtiff, libwebp and FreeType; its build docs do not mention ImageMagick. The Python binding to ImageMagick is a different library, Wand ('a ctypes-based simple ImageMagick binding for Python'). 'Best library' is opinion.
precise_version: Pillow (the maintained fork of PIL) is a popular Python library for generating images; it has its own C imaging core built on libraries like libjpeg, zlib and FreeType. ImageMagick is a separate tool, used from Python via Wand.
